headline: Q2FY27 Result Update

highlights: P&A volumes rose 29.2% YoY to 12.6 mn cases, offsetting a 5.3% decline in Mass Premium volumes Tilaknagar Industries delivered a strong Q2FY27 performance, with net revenue (adjusted for subsidy) rising 172.3% YoY to INR 1,033 cr.
Volumes reached 8.9 mn. cases (+160% YoY; +2% QoQ), while NSR increased 3.2% YoY to INR 1,174 per case.
Secondary volumes grew 8% QoQ, with Imperial Blue gaining 100 bps+ in pan-India market share, while Mansion House Reserve Brandy recorded 50% YoY volume growth in September.

Gross profit stood at INR 432 cr., with gross margin at 41.8% (-32 bps QoQ), impacted by adverse state mix and inflation across packaging materials, particularly glass, and ENA, partly offset by supply-chain efficiencies and cost optimisation.
valuation: Integration of Imperial Blue continued to progress, with over 90% of volumes now under TI operations and only one state remaining under TSMA, targeted for transition by Q4FY27.
Net debt increased to INR 2,074 cr. from INR 1,911 cr. in March 2026, with management targeting net debt below March 2026 levels by year-end.

Driven by continued market-share gains, Imperial Blue integration, cost optimisation and premiumisation, TI targets high-single to low-double-digit volume growth in FY27, with revenue growth of 200–250 bps above volume growth.

Risks to our estimates - Slower-than-expected margin accretion due to sustained packaging and ENA cost inflation, delayed price hikes and slower realisation of integration-led synergies.
